title: Why Does Your Foot Fall ASLEEP? 🦶
description:
You sit cross-legged for twenty minutes, stand up... and your leg is gone. Then comes the fizz: pins and needles.

It isn't really your circulation. Sitting like that squashes a nerve, and the tiny blood vessels that feed it. Starved, the nerve stops sending signals, so your brain can't feel the foot or tell where it is. When you move, blood rushes back and the nerve's fibres fire by themselves for a minute or two: scientists have recorded them firing in bursts of up to 300 impulses a second, with nothing touching the skin. Your brain reads that static as pins and needles. Subscribe for a new strange question every day.

It is harmless when it passes in a few minutes. Numbness or tingling that lasts, or keeps coming back for no reason, is one for a doctor.
